content: The accepted mitigation for a reader seeing a torn/partial file is writer-side: write the full content to a unique temp file in the SAME directory, fsync, then rename() over the target. rename() is atomic on a single filesystem, so a concurrent reader sees either the entire old content or the entire new content, never a mix. Without it, a reader mid-write sees partial data. Caveats: the guarantee does not hold across filesystems; on Windows rename-over-existing can throw EPERM/EACCES/EEXIST, and the common fallback (unlink target, then rename) opens a window in which the target DOES NOT EXIST, so a concurrent reader gets ENOENT rather than a torn read. Temp files created in the watched directory also generate spurious watcher events and can be mistaken for real files by a directory-globbing reader.
